name: Virginia

sales.rateNote: State retail sales and use tax of 4.3% (Code of Virginia 58.1-603) plus a 1% local tax levied by every city and county, giving the 5.3% general rate that applies in most of Virginia. Regional add-ons raise it to 6% (Central Virginia, Hampton Roads, Northern Virginia), 6.3% (eight southside localities) or 7% (Historic Triangle).

local.levies: every city and county (1% local option, 58.1-605) plus regional taxes in Northern Virginia, Hampton Roads, Central Virginia, the Historic Triangle and certain southside localities
local.capNote: The general local tax is 1%; regional taxes on top bring the combined general rate to a maximum of 7% (James City County, Williamsburg, York County).

groceries.note: Since January 1, 2023 there is no state tax on food for home consumption and essential personal hygiene products; only the 1% local tax remains, so groceries are taxed at 1% throughout Virginia. Hot prepared food is fully taxable.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the August sales tax holiday ($100 or less per item).

otherRates.item: food for home consumption and essential personal hygiene products
otherRates.note: Local 1% only; the state portion was eliminated on January 1, 2023.

holidays2026.name: Virginia's 3-Day Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: school supplies $20 or less per item; clothing and footwear $100 or less; portable generators $1,000 or less; gas chainsaws $350 or less; chainsaw accessories and other hurricane items $60 or less; Energy Star and WaterSense products for home use $2,500 or less

useTax.note: Consumer use tax at the same rate as sales tax where the item is used (5.3% in most localities, higher in regional-tax areas).

facts.text: Virginia's holiday combines back-to-school, hurricane preparedness and Energy Star items in one weekend: the first Friday to Sunday in August.
Essential personal hygiene products (such as diapers and feminine hygiene products) get the same 1% rate as groceries.
Nonprescription drugs and proprietary medicines are exempt, not just prescriptions.
Rates range from 5.3% to 7% depending on the locality; the 7% rate applies in James City County, Williamsburg and York County.
Eight southside localities, including Danville and Pittsylvania County, charge 6.3%.

property.levied: local only (counties, cities and towns); no state real estate tax

assessment.text: Real estate is assessed at 100% of fair market value. Counties must reassess every four years (or three by board vote; counties of 50,000 or fewer people may choose five or six years); many cities reassess annually.

homestead.name: No general homestead exemption
homestead.text: Virginia has no statewide homestead exemption for all owners. Localities may adopt exemptions or deferrals for owners aged 65+ or permanently and totally disabled, on conditions they set by ordinance.
homestead.applyBy: Apply with the local commissioner of the revenue or assessor under the locality's ordinance.

otherRelief.name: Disabled veteran exemption
otherRelief.text: Full exemption of the principal residence of a veteran rated 100% service-connected, permanent and total disability (constitutional exemption since 2011).

otherRelief.name: Elderly and disabled tax relief (local option)
otherRelief.text: Localities may grant exemptions, deferrals or both to owners 65+ or permanently disabled who live in the home, with income and net worth limits set locally.

facts.text: Assessment at 100% of fair market value is required by state law for every general reassessment.
Small counties (50,000 people or fewer) can stretch reassessments to every five or six years, so assessed values may lag the market.
A 100% disabled veteran's home is fully exempt, including property held jointly with a spouse.
Senior and disability relief is a local choice, so its amount and income limits differ between localities.

uncertain: Grocery treatment: state portion is 0% and the 1% local tax applies; recorded as 'exempt' (state) with groceriesTaxedLocally true. Could also be modelled as 'reduced' at 1%.
Motor vehicle sales and use tax (administered by the DMV) not verified.
Property tax due dates are set by each locality; no statewide schedule (dueDates null).
The size of each regional add-on was not read separately; only the combined rates (5.3%, 6%, 6.3%, 7%) published by Virginia Tax are used.
No change to the 4.3% state rate in 2025-2026 was found on Virginia Tax's pages.
